main_body: A pew seen from the side (east-facing): a tall brown backrest plank on the left and a seat with a red cushion panel on the right, with a bench base below.
top_band: Seat top: only a 2-row light brown band (rows 14-15, #b77246) at the top edge of the cushion panel, which is the same family as the frame; no real horizontal surface visible from above. The backrest column (x=5) is a plain vertical plank with no top band.
evidence: The drawing is a side profile of a pew: a tall vertical backrest plank beside a seat block. The seat is a red cushion panel drawn face-on, in two stacked red rectangles split by a brown band, so it reads as a vertical face. The scan at x=8 and x=11 shows a 2-row light rim (rows 14-15), then red from row 16 to 38 with a thin brown divider. That is a rim only, not a seat surface seen from above. There is no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no recess. The 2px rim is below the 3/4 threshold, so this fails as a side elevation like the guide's red side-elevation chair.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. Flat-fill coverage is 22% against 0-13%. The red cushion panels are large flat fills with no grain or highlight dots. The wood has only about 3 tones and there is no texture. The outline is a dark brown tint (2% neutral), which is fine, but the shading is shallow and the piece is much thinner than the references.
